title: LaCl3-based sodium halide solid electrolytes with high ionic conductivity for all-solid-state batteries
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    To enable high performance of all solid-state batteries, a catholyte should demonstrate high ionic conductivity, good compressibility and oxidative stability. Here, a LaCl
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    -based Na
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    superionic conductor (Na
                    <jats:sub>1</jats:sub>
                    <jats:sub>−</jats:sub>
                    <jats:sub>
                      <jats:italic>x</jats:italic>
                    </jats:sub>
                    Zr
                    <jats:sub>
                      <jats:italic>x</jats:italic>
                    </jats:sub>
                    La
                    <jats:sub>1</jats:sub>
                    <jats:sub>−</jats:sub>
                    <jats:sub>
                      <jats:italic>x</jats:italic>
                    </jats:sub>
                    Cl
                    <jats:sub>4</jats:sub>
                    ) with high ionic conductivity of 2.9 × 10
                    <jats:sup>−4 </jats:sup>
                    S cm
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    (30 °C), good compressibility and high oxidative potential (3.80 V
                    <jats:italic>vs</jats:italic>
                    . Na
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    Sn) is prepared via solid state reaction combining mechanochemical method. X-ray diffraction reveals a hexagonal structure (
                    <jats:italic>P6</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>
                      <jats:italic>3</jats:italic>
                    </jats:sub>
                    <jats:italic>/m</jats:italic>
                    ) of Na
                    <jats:sub>1</jats:sub>
                    <jats:sub>−</jats:sub>
                    <jats:sub>
                      <jats:italic>x</jats:italic>
                    </jats:sub>
                    Zr
                    <jats:sub>
                      <jats:italic>x</jats:italic>
                    </jats:sub>
                    La
                    <jats:sub>1</jats:sub>
                    <jats:sub>−</jats:sub>
                    <jats:sub>
                      <jats:italic>x</jats:italic>
                    </jats:sub>
                    Cl
                    <jats:sub>4</jats:sub>
                    , with Na
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    ions forming a one-dimensional diffusion channel along the
                    <jats:italic>c-</jats:italic>
                    axis. First-principle calculations combining with X-ray absorption fine structure characterization etc. reveal that the ionic conductivity of Na
                    <jats:sub>1</jats:sub>
                    <jats:sub>−</jats:sub>
                    <jats:sub>
                      <jats:italic>x</jats:italic>
                    </jats:sub>
                    Zr
                    <jats:sub>
                      <jats:italic>x</jats:italic>
                    </jats:sub>
                    La
                    <jats:sub>1</jats:sub>
                    <jats:sub>−</jats:sub>
                    <jats:sub>
                      <jats:italic>x</jats:italic>
                    </jats:sub>
                    Cl
                    <jats:sub>4</jats:sub>
                    is mainly determined by the size of Na
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    -channels and the Na
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    /La
                    <jats:sup>3+</jats:sup>
                    mixing in the one-dimensional diffusion channels. When applied as a catholyte, the NaCrO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ||Na
                    <jats:sub>0.7</jats:sub>
                    Zr
                    <jats:sub>0.3</jats:sub>
                    La
                    <jats:sub>0.7</jats:sub>
                    Cl
                    <jats:sub>4</jats:sub>
                    ||Na
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    PS
                    <jats:sub>4</jats:sub>
                    ||Na
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    Sn all-solid-state batteries demonstrate an initial capacity of 114 mA h g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    and 88% retention after 70 cycles at 0.3 C. In addition, a high capacity of 94 mA h g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    can be maintained at 1 C current density.
